title: BALD Base liquidity exit, cross-chain return and reported exchange endpoint
summary: Private evidence packet reconstructing the Base BALD liquidity exit, the 7,000 ETH Base-to-Ethereum withdrawal, and two subsequent 2,000 ETH + 100 ETH transfers to one Ethereum address. The bridge leg is protocol-correlated. The exchange endpoint association is a hypothesis derived from a single Lookonchain report plus amount/time/address alignment; it is not a verified exchange-cluster attribution, identity, intent, or proof of sale.

claims.text: ChainCatcher reports, citing Lookonchain monitoring, that the BALD deployer bridged 7,000 ETH from Base to Ethereum and deposited 2,100 ETH into Kraken on 2023-08-14.

gaps: No independent public provider label, exchange-cluster source, or exchange-side record ties 0xF250B3F1bb3a4d1d502C9016aF69E9976Cef0437 to Kraken.
The direct Lookonchain source post was not independently retained; ChainCatcher is a secondary report quoting it.
No human identity, key control, intent, legal conclusion, investor-loss total, or complete BALD proceeds accounting is established.
No exact-coin provenance exists between the bridge return and later ETH outputs; the temporal same-address relationship remains a hypothesis.
counterexamples: The explorer tag “Bald: Deployer” and media wording identify an address role, not the key controller or a person.

The exact 2,000 ETH and 100 ETH transfers terminate at 0xF250B3F1bb3a4d1d502C9016aF69E9976Cef0437. The independent Blockscout address record has no public name or tags; the match to the report’s Kraken destination is not independently anchored.

The 7,000 ETH bridge return and later 2,100 ETH outflows are same-address temporal/account-balance continuity only. ETH is fungible and the case does not prove that the particular bridged units were the later units transferred.
The Base receipt records returned BALD and WETH token transfers in the liquidity-removal transaction; those log quantities alone do not establish fiat proceeds, investor loss, or intent.
The reported exchange destination does not identify a Kraken customer/account or show that funds were sold.

caveats: Same-address balance continuity and report amount/date align, but intervening balance history and ETH fungibility prevent tracing the same coin units.
The recipient 0xF250… is unlabeled in the retained independent Blockscout address metadata.

source_disagreements: The secondary report attributes 2,100 ETH to Kraken, while captured chain transactions show 2,000 ETH and 100 ETH sent to an unlabeled 0xF250… address. Amounts and date align, but the destination label is not independently corroborated by the captured chain/provider data.
